question: Does a planning key digesting a compact binary writing of the position, instead of its canonical text, leave play unchanged, and what does it save?
machine: Apple M4 Max: 10 performance and 4 efficiency cores, 36 GB
tool: tools/compare_engine_builds.py, identifying positions by canonical key

keys_in_one_searched_game.how: a build of 525a542 counting key computations and menu table lookups (src/campaign_runtime.cpp, src/campaign_state.cpp), one searched game

profile_before.how: /usr/bin/sample, 60 s of searched game 41 from 25 s after it started, on 525a542

key_microseconds.how: positions of a random game (seed 7) every 150 steps, each key 200 times, one thread

notes: Searched games are compared by each event's kind and move and the final canonical key, because planning keys differ between the builds.

The bracketed trio ran in the order: this change, the slot maps build, this change. The Mac's other work peaked at a five-minute load average near 18 during it, so CPU seconds are rough; instruction counts of repeated runs of one build differ by about 1%.
